experiments.scope: Reduced-width test of H1 at claim-shaped budgets: width 12 bits, fresh budget 66, total 258. Tests the truncated function only; the step to 256 bits is the extrapolation stated in proof.md Section 8.
experiments.hypothesis: Program check at width 12: the Section 3 algorithm with fresh budget M=66 (M^2/2^13=0.5317 against 0.5213 in the claim, the rounding of M up to an integer), theta=2^-2, L_max=64, total budget 258, run on the three-round digest truncated to its first 12 bits, returns a host-verified 12-bit-prefix collision in a fraction of trials consistent with that of a uniformly random 12-bit function. Reference measured by the author over 10,000 trials with a fresh random function per trial: q=0.3357 (99% CI [0.3236, 0.3480]); 20 fixed random instances of 2,000 trials: mean 0.3360, sd 0.0377, range [0.2825, 0.4125]. Predicted successes in 256 trials: 85.9. Author comparison floor: 67, the 0.5% quantile of Binomial(256, q). A count below 67 would send the author back to the program and to F_w at this width; a count at or above 67 says that the program runs under the executor and finds host-verifiable pairs at a rate consistent with a random function at this width. Neither outcome is evidence about width 256, and no claimed number depends on this count. The author's own 256-seed run returned 83; the organizer's seeds differ. Only the returned pairs are host-verified; observations are participant counters. See proof.md Section 8.

experiments.scope: Unbudgeted run at width 16 (hard stop 2^20 steps): checks that the shipped search finds a host-verifiable 16-bit-prefix collision of the three-round digest in every trial, and reports step counts (untrusted) for comparison with the birthday prediction.
experiments.hypothesis: Every trial returns a pair of distinct 64-byte messages of the family 0^32 || x whose three-round digests agree on the first 16 bits (256 of 256 expected; any trial returning no pair would indicate a defect in the search or a function on which the walk cannot find a collision within 2^20 steps). Author's run: 256 of 256, mean 346.9 total steps against a random-function prediction of about 345, median 331, max 1029. Observations are participant counters and are not host-verified. See proof.md Section 8.
